name: read-access-during-session
body:
While a session owns `apg/.trans/db.lbug` with an exclusive lock, a reader must still be able to see the current state — but ONLY by routing through the live session. The coordinator owns the DB for the duration of the session; reads are served by routing to that session over the same transparent socket as writes (`apg query` / the suite query tools detect the live session and forward the read). Such a routed read returns the post-mutation state immediately, with no lock error and no waiting for the session to end.

A NON-routing reader — one that opens `db.lbug` directly instead of routing, or whose session detection/connect fails (e.g. a stale-but-present socket) — is OUT of contract while a session is live. lbug's contended open ERRORS ("Could not set lock … Resource temporarily unavailable") rather than waits, so the only correct behaviours are to route via the tool or to be retried after the session ends; a direct contended open is not a supported alternative and must not be implied.

When NO session is live (the direct path), the DB file is not held, and any reader opens it normally and sees committed mutations — that is the `read-your-writes` guarantee. Read-through routing applies only while a session is live.

This requirement constrains the observable behaviour, not the mechanism: it guarantees a routed reader immediate visibility and does not promise that a non-routing direct opener succeeds during a session.

Acceptance: with a live session that has applied a mutation, a separate `apg query` process (routed through the session) returns the post-mutation state with no lock error and without waiting for the session to end; after the session ends, a fresh `apg query` process opens the DB directly and returns the same state.
